current_heading: Independent steps with equal duration and variance give linear variance growth

evidence: The complete connected explanation at lines 159-218 was read, including fixed 2D Delta t increments, the sum, Brownian interpretation, bias example, figure connection, covariance and boundary limits.

For n independent steps of equal duration Delta t and equal variance sigma squared, variance of the sum is n sigma squared = (sigma squared / Delta t)t. Thus the revised title includes the missing condition.
The prior counterexample has variance j in step j and violates the new equal-variance premise, so it no longer contradicts the title.
The body still explicitly assumes mean zero for the MSD equality. The revised title claims variance growth only, for which zero mean is not required.
The sidecar title matches the source. No changed body meaning or new claim was introduced by the title repair.
